findings.claim: The fallback launcher write can follow the real Corepack shim symlink and overwrite the globally installed Corepack pnpm launcher; disposable-root cleanup then leaves the host launcher broken.
proof_refs: Real `corepack enable pnpm --install-directory <private-bin>` creates `<private-bin>/pnpm` as a symlink to the globally installed `corepack/dist/pnpm.js`.

After classified `corepack prepare` failure, `createPnpmExecLauncher` calls `writeFile(<private-bin>/pnpm, ...)` without unlink, exclusive creation, or no-follow containment, so the write follows that symlink.
Removing the disposable root removes only the private symlink and does not restore the overwritten global Corepack launcher.
The defect violates R3 no ambient authority, R4 bounded cleanup/repetition, and R5 fail-closed fallback launcher.

findings.claim: The tests do not exercise a real Corepack-created shim before fallback launcher creation.
proof_refs: The fallback tests stub `runCommand`; none invokes real `corepack enable --install-directory <private-bin>` and verifies that global launcher bytes remain unchanged.

findings.claim: The fallback classifier may treat a mixed error containing a compatibility phrase plus a network, timeout, integrity, extraction, or platform failure as fallback-eligible.
proof_refs: Classification is a positive phrase regex over concatenated message and stderr, without explicit denial when disallowed failure classes are also present.

findings.claim: Fallback launcher materialization writes through the real Corepack-generated symlink into global `corepack/dist/pnpm.js`, damaging host state outside the disposable boundary and surviving cleanup.
proof_refs: A real `corepack enable pnpm --install-directory <private-bin>` installs a symlink targeting globally installed `corepack/dist/pnpm.js`.
Fallback reuses the same pathname with ordinary `writeFile`, which follows the symlink and overwrites the global target.
Temporary-root cleanup cannot restore the host target, contradicting isolation, cleanup, and fail-closed requirements R3/R4/R5.

findings.claim: R11 wording requires one combined rollback while the planned chain documents separate U1 and U2 rollback boundaries and ordering constraints.
proof_refs: The requirement says rollback removes private pnpm provisioning and tests together with both resolutions and lock entries.
The chain separately defines U1 and U2 rollback operations and forbids removing U1 after U2 exists except as part of the complete candidate.
